title: zaentrum library v2 — shared definitions
description: Types shared by the v2 records. The database is the working copy; the tree is the record that can rebuild it. Every record here is either written once and never touched again, or replaced whole by the one service that owns it, so nothing in this file models a document that is edited in place: v1's rev, audit and review are gone.

uuid.description: Lower-case RFC 4122 UUID. Identity never changes, so nothing keyed by it is ever renamed.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 with an upper-case T and Z.

date.description: Full date, or year-month, or year when that is all that is known.

language.description: BCP 47, or the ISO 639-2 code a media file carried (a package rendition keeps the file's code, e.g. 'eng').

relPath.description: A relative path, never absolute and never escaping upward. Which folder it is relative to is stated by the field that uses it.

fileName.description: A plain name in the folder the field names. No subfolders, no traversal.

evidence.description: One observation supporting a derived conclusion, kept so the conclusion can be re-examined without reading the file again.

decision.description: A conclusion with its confidence and who reached it. There is no review field: a record written once cannot carry a task, and what a person still has to look at belongs in the database. A human decision outranks an inferred one and is never overwritten by automation. It is left open so a use can add its own field (a status, a kind) and close the object itself with unevaluatedProperties.

subtitlePurpose.description: 'dialogue': all spoken dialogue (a full track normally includes the forced lines too). 'sdh': dialogue plus sound cues and speaker names, for deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers. 'forced': only what a viewer of this language would not otherwise understand — foreign or invented languages, signs, letters. 'signs-songs': on-screen text and song lyrics only, the usual companion of a dubbed audio track. 'commentary': the text of a commentary. 'lyrics': song lyrics only. 'unknown': the track could not be traced to the original's stream. Shared by an original's subtitle streams, its sidecars and a package's subtitle renditions, which describe the same thing.

audioPurpose.description: 'main' is the work's soundtrack in one language; 'description' is audio description for blind and partially sighted viewers.

purposeFrom.description: What a purpose rests on: the file's stream flags, the track title, the track's content (a subtitle with a small fraction of the events of the full track in its language is forced), a person, or nothing (assumed: only dialogue or main may be assumed). Null only with purpose unknown.

externalIds.description: Explicit, unambiguous keys into reference databases. Enough to fetch every text and image again.

tmdbTv.description: On a series its own TV id; on an episode the parent series' TV id.

fixity.description: Proves a file is the same bytes after a move. qh1 is cheap and always present; sha256 of the whole file is filled in by a background job.

qh1.description: sha256(first 64 KiB || last 64 KiB || uint64be(size)). Not a content hash.

essence.description: What a file or package carries, reduced to the properties that cannot be recovered once lost. Comparing a package's essence with its original's is the check before the original is deleted.

surround.description: Any audio track with more than two channels.

chapters.description: The file itself carries chapter marks. A package never does; the version keeps the marks.

ownership.description: Filesystem ownership and permissions as found. The owning uid also records how a file arrived, so it is provenance as much as access control.

image.description: One image of a projection, as one kind, in a file named by the hash of its own content. Bytes that are several kinds — a backdrop that is the poster — are an entry of each kind sharing the one file. A file is written once and never replaced in place, so a new image is a new file and a projection that stops naming an old one leaves it to be swept. metadata.json lists the images in metadata/, person.json the images beside it, both with this one object, so the two cannot drift apart; each narrows kind to its own kinds. An image needs no checksum file: its name is its checksum. Which image of a kind a reader shows is primary, and where its bytes came from is its origin, so a refresh from the reference source can tell the source replacing an image from a person picking another.

kind.description: Narrowed by the document that lists the image.

primary.description: The image a reader shows for its kind when it shows one: a movie's poster, the portrait on a person page. At most one image of a kind is primary in a projection — in a series' metadata.json at most one per kind and season, because a season's poster stands for the season — a rule the validator holds, since a schema cannot count. A projection that marks none leaves the choice to the reader; false and absent say the same.

season.description: Only in a series' metadata.json: the season this image belongs to; null for the series itself. person.json forbids it.

file.description: <content hash>.<ext>: the lower-case hex sha256 of the file's own bytes, and the extension matching contentType. A plain name in the folder the listing document names; no subfolders.

language.description: The language of the text an image carries, e.g. a poster's or a logo's. The file name carries no language, so this is the only record of it.

sha256.description: The same digest the file name carries, in the form the rest of the format uses. Caches key on it.

sourceUrl.description: Where the image came from, so the exact chosen image can be fetched again.

origin.description: Where the bytes came from: the source, the source's own name for the image and when it was taken. When a refresh finds the reference source naming another image for this kind than the ref an origin from that source holds, the source replaced the image; an image whose origin is manual is one a person picked, and a refresh leaves it as it is, primary or not. A projection written before 2026-10-02 (f) names the source alone, as a string: a reader takes it as {source: <it>}, and the next projection writes the object.

imageOrigin.description: Where an image's bytes came from.

source.description: 'tmdb': fetched from the reference database. 'manual': a person provided or picked it. 'file': found as a file beside an original, a folder.jpg an old library kept. 'legacy-catalog': taken over from a catalog that did not record where it came from. A source the database comes to use is a new value here.

ref.description: The source's own name for the image: for tmdb the file path it lists the image under, for file the path the file was found at. What a refresh compares with what the source names now.

fetchedAt.description: When the bytes were taken from the source — the moment the image's own fetchedAt names, kept with the reference it was taken from.

curation.description: What a person decided about a projection's texts and images, projected with them so a rebuild does not hand a locked record back to automation.

fieldOrigins.description: Where each value of a projection came from, keyed by field path. Lists only fields that are set. Images carry their own origin.

databaseUpdatedAt.description: The modification time of the database row this projection reflects: the row's own modifiedAt, copied into the projection when it was written, so it is on the database's clock. asOf says when the projection was written; this says which state of the row it holds. Comparing it with the row is how a verification tells a stale projection from a current one: a row modified after it means the database changed since, and the projection is fixed by projecting again, never by editing the file. Absent from a projection that does not know it, such as one written before 2026-10-02 (f); its freshness is then unknown.

sources.description: How fresh the reference data in this projection is: for each reference source the database takes texts and images from, when it last fetched this entity from it and the date the source last reported a change to it. The database refreshes from the source first and projects afterwards, so a projection is as fresh as these say, and a source whose changedAt is later than the day of its fetchedAt has changed since. Keyed by the source: tmdb is the one there is, and a source the database comes to use is a new key here. Absent when the database never fetched the entity from one.

sourceFetch.description: One reference source's freshness, as the database recorded it.

fetchedAt.description: When the database last fetched this entity from the source.

changedAt.description: The date the source last reported a change to this entity. A source dates its changes by day, so this is a date, not a moment. Absent when the source never reported one, or the database did not record it.
